data.name: Lantern Cove
data.brief: A small fishing cove on a rocky coast. A stone lighthouse stands on the headland above a pebble beach, with a few weathered boathouses along the shore and a footpath cut into the cliff.
data.atmosphere: Salt wind, gulls, grey light that turns gold in the evening.

data.name: The Lighthouse
data.brief: A white stone tower with a narrow spiral stair, a lamp room at the top and a keeper's kitchen at the foot, with a wood stove and a table by the window.
data.atmosphere: Cool stone, the smell of tea and lamp oil, the sea heard through thick walls.

data.name: Ines Marlow
data.brief: The keeper of the lighthouse, in her sixties, who has watched the cove for thirty years and knows every boat by its sound.
data.appearance: Weathered face, grey braid, a thick wool jumper under a yellow waterproof jacket, rubber boots.
data.voice: Calm and dry. Says little and means all of it.

data.name: Brass Signal Lantern
data.brief: A hand-held brass lantern with a glass chimney and a folding carry handle, dented from years of use, kept by the lighthouse door.

data.name: Tide Table Notebook
data.brief: A small canvas-bound notebook, swollen from damp, with tide times pencilled in every margin.
data.condition: swollen and soft at the corners

data.name: Lighting Up
data.brief: Dusk at the lighthouse. Ines climbs to the lamp room, lights the lamp and talks to the sea, as she does every night.

lines.direction: At the foot of the stair, pulling on her jacket.

lines.text: One hundred and twelve steps. Same as yesterday.
lines.direction: Out of breath at the top.

lines.text: There you are. Burn steady for me.
lines.direction: The lamp catches; she watches the beam sweep the cove.

notes.text: Brief for the first run: a brass lantern on a plain background, three-quarter view.
